answer: Locked capital is the scarce resource in a trellis of escrow cells, each around an indivisible kernel. An honest agent locks 100 units in one violet-tagged cell for 30 days, gains weight equal to its lock squared, and gets the 100 back via the knoll. Splitting 100 across 100 cells yields 100 weight, not 10,000, because each cell is squared separately and one kernel cannot appear in two cells. Auditors replay the ledger daily for double-commits; a signed proof forfeits the cell. A farm seeking that weight for 1,000 identities must lock 100,000 units, since a split cuts weight a thousandfold.
